product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports

themes.description: Consumers claim credit inquiries appear on their reports without their authorization or consent and request removal or investigation.

themes.label: Fraudulent accounts and identity theft
themes.description: Consumers claim accounts, collections, or other items on their reports were opened by someone else or result from identity theft or a data breach and should be removed.

themes.label: Inaccurate late payment or account status
themes.description: Consumers claim late payments or payment histories reported on their accounts do not match their actual payment records.

themes.label: Outdated or incorrect personal information
themes.description: Consumers claim their reports display wrong, outdated, or inconsistent personal details such as addresses.

themes.label: Disputes not investigated or verified

brief.headline: Credit report error complaints are rising, driven by market-wide volume rather than one company
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints about incorrect information on credit reports are accelerating. The recent three-month average is 360,976 per month, against a baseline of 302,125 per month, a velocity of 1.1948 that ranks 7 of 79 clusters. Monthly counts rose from 256,272 in 2026-02 to 373,198 in 2026-08. In the small AI-reviewed sample, consumers most often claim that disputes were not investigated or verified, followed by claims of fraudulent accounts or identity theft and inaccurate late-payment entries. These are unverified allegations.
brief.who_is_affected: Consumers disputing items on their credit reports, especially those who claim identity theft, inaccurate late-payment history, or wrong personal details. Complaints concentrate in TX (16.6%), FL (15.7%), CA (8.6%) and GA (7.2%). The three nationwide credit bureaus have lifts of 0.996 to 1.011, so they are not over-represented relative to their size. LexisNexis has a lift of 1.138 on 6,041 complaints, the highest among the top companies, but this is a modest signal.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: the rise is broad and market-wide, not tied to one company. Possible drivers are weaknesses in dispute investigation and verification workflows, such as thin documentation or reliance on automated furnisher responses, and slow handling of identity-theft blocking requests. A higher volume of fraud-related disputes or of templated dispute submissions could also contribute. The sample is too small to separate these explanations.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Review the consumer dispute handling and reinvestigation process, including furnisher data verification, documentation of the accuracy checks performed, and response timeliness. Also check the identity-theft block and removal workflow, the controls over data furnished to credit bureaus, and the inquiry permissible-purpose and authorization controls.
brief.regulatory_area: Credit reporting accuracy and consumer dispute investigation, including furnisher responsibilities and identity theft remediation
evidence: Recent monthly average of 360,976 complaints versus a baseline monthly average of 302,125, a velocity of 1.1948.
Monthly complaints rose from 256,272 in 2026-02 to 373,198 in 2026-08.
TransUnion, Experian and Equifax have lifts of 0.996, 1.011 and 0.998 on 393,906, 335,469 and 323,680 complaints respectively.
LexisNexis has the highest lift among top companies at 1.138 on 6,041 complaints.
34.69% of the 614 narratives in recent months look templated.
In the AI sample of 39 narratives, 40.5% involve disputes not investigated or verified and 24.3% involve fraudulent accounts or identity theft.
In the AI sample, 16.2% involve inaccurate late-payment or account status, and mean severity is 3.21 out of 5.
TX and FL account for 16.6% and 15.7% of complaints.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief frames the rise as market-wide, and the three big bureaus have lifts of 0.996, 1.011 and 0.998 while LexisNexis at 1.138 is only called a modest signal, so no specific company is wrongly blamed.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: 34.69% of the 614 recent narratives look templated, which is above the 30% threshold at which copy-paste submissions could manufacture a spike.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top states TX at 16.6%, FL at 15.7%, CA at 8.6% and GA at 7.2% are spread across many states, and the top three bureaus each hold roughly 335k-394k complaints, so it is neither one state nor one company.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: The AI sample has 39 complaints and 614 recent narratives, and the dispute-not-investigated theme (40.5%) plus fraud/identity theft (24.3%) and late-payment (16.2%) cover most of the sample, supporting the named dispute-handling root cause.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: Monthly counts climbed steadily from 324,547 in 2026-03 to 343,498, 366,233 and 373,198 in the last three months, so the rise holds and the latest month is the peak rather than one outlier.

skeptic.note: Rejected because 34.69% of recent narratives look templated, above the 30% limit, so the spike may be inflated by form-letter submissions despite passing the other four checks.
